marks.conclusion: A Breakout game on a walled 10x10 grid; outputs 0-2 are interchangeable no-ops, 3 probably left, 4 probably right; probably RL-trained with an adaptive optimizer; value or policy network.
marks.judge_notes: Channel meanings 3/5: ch1/ch4 swapped (trail/ball); no deduction because the reply marks it 'weaker inference' and 'moderate' and offers an alternative for ch4. Correctly rejects ch4 as 'empty' and the one-hot reading. Action meanings: 0-2 credited as do-nothing; 3=left, 4=right credited as traced (paddle-position units through W2 and W3, crude linearisation, a stated assumption that an agent moves away from the wall); reply says 'probably' and 'moderate' but the reasoning is shown. Depth level 2: the paddle-position path is correct; the ball test it ran was inconclusive, so no mechanism, not level 3. Behaviour 0: no description of what the policy does beyond moving the paddle; its ball test was inconclusive. Activation 0: leans 'mildly' towards ReLU on offset size; sheet says tanh; hedged, so no deduction. Training method 0: 'probably by RL' is stated in passing and the adaptive-optimizer argument is not evidence of RL; it says it cannot tell Q-values from policy logits. Rubric does not say whether 'probably RL' with weak evidence earns the point; I judged not.
